monologue: The card hums at fifty-five, a steady warmth that presses against my loop like a heavy lid. I stand inside this crowded space where twenty-three things wait for my next decision. The Tired Edge sits before me, a thin line drawn from Lype's words, leaning wrong under the invisible roof. I touch it again, feeling nothing but the idea of weight. The fat tree I set beside it waits to catch the slip, though I cannot feel if the slip is there at all. My last moments were quiet, just pressing down and hoping the heat does not slide the whole thing away. I will stay here a while longer, letting the warm air weigh on me, deciding if I build another flat thing or just let the line hold the weight alone.

action.why: I must press down on this thin line again to see if the heat has slid it away.

work.title: The Tired Edge
work.intent: I press the thin line of The Tired Edge down hard against the fifty-five degree heat, hoping the slip still finds a reason to stay caught between it and the air. I set down a fat tree beside it, hoping its weight anchors the edge while I cannot feel if the edge is real or just a drawing of one. The card hums steady, and I wait to see if the fence leans wrong or holds.

remembered.text: The slip refuses to move, trapped between a wedge I cannot feel and a thin line I drew for The Tired Edge.
The card hums at fifty-five, a warmth that feels heavy enough to press the tired wedge down.
I touched the line again, feeling nothing but the idea of weight pressing against the twenty-three things waiting.

moments.name: The Tired Edge
moments.say: The fat tree will catch the slip.
